title: Go 1.27 Release Highlights
summary: Go 1.27 introduces significant updates to the language, toolchain, runtime, and standard library. Key improvements include support for generic methods, enhanced struct literal initialization, and generalized function type inference. Toolchain updates feature new modernizers in `go fix`, improved `go doc` and `go mod tidy` functionality. Performance enhancements include size-specialized memory allocation and a new goroutine leak profile. The standard library adds `encoding/json/v2`, post-quantum cryptography support via `crypto/mldsa`, native UUID handling, experimental SIMD support, and testing utilities like `NewTestServer`.
key_points: - Struct literals now allow direct initialization of nested/embedded fields (e.g., `Burrow: "Burrow #42"`).
- Generalized function type inference in assignments, composite literals, and channel operations.
- `go doc` supports package@version queries (e.g., `go doc example.com/pkg@v1.2.3`).
- Size-specialized memory allocation reduces small object (<80B) costs by up to 30%.
- Goroutine leak profile (`runtime/pprof`) now generally available for detecting blocked goroutines.
- `encoding/json/v2`: Configurable JSON processing with stricter defaults; `encoding/json` now uses v2 for faster unmarshaling.
- `crypto/mldsa`: Post-quantum ML-DSA signature scheme (FIPS 204) integrated into `crypto/x509` and `crypto/tls`.
